title: Week 40: Profiling and Runtime Performance Checkpoint

questions.prompt: Checkpoint: What should every performance number include?
questions.explanation: The exact journey, metric, device/environment, app/data state, compilation/build state and measurement method. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
options: Define representative user impact and controlled evidence before changing the measured critical path.
Optimise the largest method by intuition
questions.answer: Define representative user impact and controlled evidence before changing the measured critical path.

questions.prompt: Select the two sound practices for cpu profiler, perfetto, and trace interpretation.
questions.explanation: Thread scheduling state, child work and system events aligned with the app slice. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
options: Use time-aligned system and app slices to distinguish running, blocked and scheduled causes on the user critical path.
Record representative evidence and an owned recovery action
answer: Use time-aligned system and app slices to distinguish running, blocked and scheduled causes on the user critical path.
Record representative evidence and an owned recovery action

questions.prompt: A large object in a heap dump is necessarily a memory leak.
questions.explanation: An object remains reachable through an unintended retaining path after its useful owner lifecycle has ended. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.

questions.prompt: Complete the operational rule: Why does display refresh rate matter to jank analysis?
questions.explanation: Higher refresh rates provide a smaller time budget before each frame deadline. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
questions.answer: Higher refresh rates provide a smaller time budget before each frame deadline.
acceptedAnswers: Higher refresh rates provide a smaller time budget before each frame deadline.

questions.prompt: Order the investigation steps for battery and network efficiency.
questions.explanation: Each request can incur scheduling, connection and radio high-power tail overhead. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
options: Name the user or release outcome
answer: Name the user or release outcome

questions.prompt: Match the review concern to its evidence for application size and delivery analysis.
questions.explanation: The device-specific APK set and installed/first-use footprint, not only the source AAB. This applies the lesson's evidence and recovery model.
options: Mechanism → direct trace or artifact evidence
